notes:
The whole collection was read — 1,165 catalogue records, not the 593 the extract issue estimated. The 593 came from `digitalsf_profile.py`, which reads the address out of `245$a` and requires a street type; SFP 23 files much of its material as "1377 Fulton", and carries a second, structured address in the archivist's `500$a` note ("Address. Box 3; Mission, 3232-3234."). Reading both fields nearly doubles the yield.

Dates come from `260$c`, not `269$a`. Where `260$c` reads "between 1946 and 1951", `269$a` reads 1946, so a pass that trusts `269$a` records an archivist's range as a firm year. 298 records are imprecise and only 115 of them are flagged `fuzzy date` in `907$a` — the flag under-reports imprecision here by more than half. Those 295 findings carry `date_precision: circa`, the phrase itself in `date`, and the endpoints in `extra.date_range`.

175 findings state an address range ("2929-2931 24th Street") and so carry no `street_number`; the range is in `extra.address_range_as_recorded` and which number the parcel takes is the resolver's call. Four state a number they are not at ("South of 500 Bayshore Boulevard") and likewise carry none. 18 give no number at all — Playland at the Beach, seven intersections, four assessor blocks, two block faces and one bare street — and are kept as unresolved findings so the next pass does not re-read them.

Names: every `700`/`710` in this collection is the corporate Office of the Assessor-Recorder and there is not one `600` personal subject, so the profiler's `named-person` flag means nothing here. The people are in the titles, on storefront signs. `extra.named_in_record` keeps the firms and drops the individuals — eighteen fragments, all of them a professional renting an office ("F. Justin McCarthy, M.D.") rather than a business — per "Privacy — hard limits" in the root AGENTS.md. `research/tools/digitalsf_extract.py --report` prints both lists.

Rights: all 1,165 records are `No Copyright – United States`. The 60%-In-Copyright figure in the dossier is a whole-repository number and does not apply to this collection. Reproducing an image still needs a human decision.

**Resolved 2026-08-15** against `sf-eas-addresses`, `sf-parcels` and the 2025 secured roll, with `research/tools/resolve_eas.py` (`--alias DOUGLAS=DOUGLASS`). 923 of 1,122 findings resolved — 82%, well above the 69% a random sample of this source predicted — onto 886 parcels and 889 paths; 165 of those paths are pages that already exist, 758 are pages that do not. 199 are unresolved, and the file keeps every one of them.

Why the 199 miss, in order of size: 74 have no EAS record at all (the address is gone); 43 are condominiums today, 25 classed so on the roll and 18 found as one active parcel per unit at the address's own point; 39 state a range whose numbers sit on several parcels now; 25 give no street number; 11 are conflicts where the title and the archivist's note are both real addresses on different parcels; 3 name a street EAS does not hold (Maritime Plaza, Stonestown, Hunt Street); 2 are in EAS with no parcel number; 2 sit on a retired parcel with no active one under them.

Three things this pass established about the collection's addressing. **The archivist's assessor block is a genuine check, not just a lead** — of the 166 findings that carry one, 156 reached a parcel to check it against and 153 agreed (one of them as the block a lettered sub-block sits in), and the three that disagree (`sfp-23-0019`, `-0834`, `-0838`) now carry a `conflict` the resolver wrote rather than inherited. **The source spells four streets its own way** — Bayshore for BAY SHORE, O'Farrell for OFARRELL, Sea Cliff for SEACLIFF, Embarcadero for THE EMBARCADERO — and one, Douglas for DOUGLASS, needed an explicit alias; unmapped they read as demolished addresses, which is the wrong answer for the wrong reason. **EAS's `parcel_number` is stale or absent often enough to matter**: 49 findings resolved only after the address's own coordinates were put through `sf-parcels` for the parcel that exists now.

The counts in `coverage.note` above are per *record*: 26 conflicts and 547/19/304/295 dates describe the 1,165 catalogue records, and the file holds 1,122 findings after 43 duplicates were folded. Per finding the same figures are 24 conflicts (27 now) and 520 day / 19 month / 296 year / 287 circa. Nothing was re-dated: the 287 circa findings keep their phrase, and 256 of them resolved to a parcel without acquiring a year.

coverage.remaining: None of SFP 23 — the collection is fully read. The other 43 DigitalSF collections are untouched; by candidate count the next ones are San Francisco Subjects Photograph Collection (SFP 162), San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Records (SFH 371) and Tenderloin Times Photograph Archives (SFP 130). Re-run `digitalsf_harvest.py` first to pick up records added since 2026-08-15.
coverage.note: Read every record in the collection: 1,165 unique catalogue records, 1,128 of which give a street number in the title, in the archivist's address note, or in both. Folding 43 duplicate photographs of the same address on the same date leaves 1,122 findings over 1,083 distinct addresses. 26 findings carry a `conflict` because the title and the address note disagree. Dates: 547 to the day, 19 to the month, 304 to the year, 295 imprecise. The dates run 1940 to 1991 and cluster in the 1950s (704) and 1940s (289), so nothing here falls under the 1909 renumbering traps in loc-newspapers.md. Nothing is resolved — every entry is `unresolved` pending the EAS check.
